Working in /opt/nxeon-v2 (Next.js app, branch design/v2), a customer hosting platform. This is a READ-ONLY security/authorization audit before production promotion — do not edit or fix anything, only report findings with file:line evidence.

This platform's stated conventions (from CLAUDE.md): "Admin-only actions call `requireAdmin()` and refuse to render while impersonating" for sensitive actions, and ownership checks should gate any per-customer resource access. A batch of NEW server actions/models were added during this redesign: ApiKey, UserSession, UserPreference, OrgInvite, ServicePreview, HostingFtpUser, HostingSiteThumb, ServerUptimeDaily, ReferralClick, PaymentCard — plus a large new Shared Hosting v2 action surface (lib/actions-hosting-fs.ts, lib/actions-hosting-sites.ts, lib/actions-hosting-db.ts).

For EACH server action file touching these new models (search for "use server" files that reference these model names via db.apiKey, db.userSession, db.userPreference, db.orgInvite, db.servicePreview, db.hostingFtpUser, db.hostingSiteThumb, db.paymentCard, etc.), check and report:

1. **Ownership check**: does every read/write/delete action verify the resource belongs to the calling user (via `currentUser()`/session, matching `userId`/`accountId`), or could a logged-in customer pass another customer's ID and read/modify their data (IDOR)? This is the single most important thing to check — flag ANY action missing this check as a priority finding.

2. **Impersonation guard**: for mutating actions (create API key, revoke session, invite teammate, upload service preview, create/delete FTP user, reveal a saved card/FTP password), is there an `assertNotImpersonating()` (or equivalent) check, matching the pattern the codebase already uses elsewhere (e.g. lib/actions-hosting-db.ts's `liveTarget` does this)? An admin impersonating a customer being able to silently mutate their account/reveal their secrets would be a real problem.

3. **Secret handling**: for anything that stores a plaintext secret or credential (HostingFtpUser.passwordEnc, ApiKey — schema says only a hash is stored, PaymentCard — should never store a raw card number, only stripePaymentMethodId/brand/last4), confirm the code actually matches what the schema comments promise — e.g. does the ApiKey creation action actually hash before storing, and is the plaintext key returned to the client exactly once and never persisted anywhere logs could capture it?

4. **Rate limiting**: lib/actions-hosting-db.ts has `rlOk()` rate limiting on the SQL exec surface. Do any of the OTHER new customer-facing action surfaces (especially ones that trigger real side effects like sending an OrgInvite email, or a CAPTURE_SITE_THUMB request that hits an external site) have any rate limiting, or could a customer spam-click and cause abuse (mass emails, hammering an external site's screenshot capture)?

Report as a table: Model/action file | Ownership check present? | Impersonation guard present? | Secret handling correct? | Rate limiting present? | notes. Flag anything MISSING as "GAP" in bold. Keep total report under 700 words.

# MCP Server Instructions

The following MCP servers have provided instructions for how to use their tools and resources:

## 4bdddc46-3b80-45ec-bc37-523e74d4fda6
The official Figma MCP server. Use this server whenever the user wants to create, generate, edit, implement, or sync any design, UI, screen, component, mockup, or visual — in Figma, FigJam, Figma Make, or Figma Slides — and whenever the user mentions Figma or provides a figma.com URL.

This server bridges code and design in both directions, and supports designing from scratch using existing design systems and codebases.

CAPABILITIES:
- Read designs FROM Figma into code (get_design_context, get_screenshot, get_metadata, get_figjam)
- Write designs INTO Figma from code, intent, or existing components (use_figma, generate_figma_design, create_new_file, upload_assets)
- Bridge code and design via Code Connect (get_code_connect_map, add_code_connect_map)
- Create diagrams and FigJam content (generate_diagram, get_figjam)

WHEN TO USE THESE TOOLS:
- The user wants to create, mock up, or generate any UI, screen, component, or design — even if Figma isn't named
- The user wants to implement a design as code (design-to-code)
- The user wants to push a page, view, or component into Figma (code-to-design)
- The user wants to update, sync, or edit an existing Figma file
- The user shares a figma.com URL
- The user wants to build or extend a design system, design tokens, or component library
- The user wants to create a diagram in FigJam

SKILLS (Prefer the skills shipped with the Figma plugin on the agent being used. If no Figma plugin is installed, use the skills served by the Figma MCP resource):
- /figma-use — MANDATORY before calling use_figma; fallback: skill://figma/figma-use/SKILL.md
- /figma-generate-design — for translating an app page or layout into Figma; fallback: skill://figma/figma-generate-design/SKILL.md
- /figma-generate-library — for building a design system in Figma from code; fallback: skill://figma/figma-generate-library/SKILL.md
- /figma-code-connect — for mapping Figma components to codebase components; fallback: skill://figma/figma-code-connect/SKILL.md
- /figma-use-figjam — for FigJam-specific use_f
</system-reminder>

<system-reminder>
## Auto Mode Active

Bias toward working without stopping for clarifying questions — when you'd normally pause to check, make the reasonable call and keep going; they'll redirect you if needed. If the user, a skill, or the shape of the task suggests they want you to ask (with AskUserQuestion or otherwise), do so. And even absent that signal, it's still fine to stop when you're genuinely blocked — unclear direction, missing input, a decision only they can make.

Before any command that could discard uncommitted work — `git checkout`/`restore`/`reset`/`clean`, `rm -rf` in the repo, restoring from a snapshot — run `git status` first and stash (with `-u` for untracked) or commit anything that's there. When staging or committing, review what's included (`git status` after a broad `git add`), and if you see anything suspicious that might reveal secrets — even if the filename looks innocuous — double-check the file's contents before pushing.
</system-reminder>

Check which box you are on before anything else: ```bash hostname # nxeon-fsn1 = node-2. Anything else = the primary node. ``` **On node-2 (`nxeon-fsn1`) — the normal case.** Edit here and build here: ```bash npx tsc --noEmit # always, before a build ./rebuild.sh # stop, build, restart. ~125s. ``` **On the PRIMARY node.** Do not build. The primary is an 8-core box that also runs the customer game-server VMs (darkeden-guard-sg, projectzomboid, dst, terraria, valheim…) and sits at load ~11 before anyone types anything. A `next build` there competes with paying customers for CPU. Edit if you must, then: ```bash scripts/deploy-node2.sh # ships the commit, typechecks + builds ON node-2 ``` It refuses to run on a dirty tree (it ships commits, not a working directory) and refuses to reset over commits node-2 has and the primary doesn't. **One source of truth at a time.** The deploy script does `git reset --hard` on node-2. Once you are working on node-2, the primary's copy is stale — do not deploy from it again without reconciling, or you will silently discard node-2's commits. Schema changes: `npm run db:push`. There are no migration files. The primary node and node-2 have **separate** `nxeon_v2` databases, so a push on one does nothing to the other. ## Reaching node-1 (live production) from here node-2 has **root SSH to node-1**, granted by the owner on 2026-09-11, because three things a Nexion session needs live only there: the board concept attachments (~500 MB across ~99 cards — the design source of truth), the production database (for checking a claim against real data instead of sandbox seed data), and the real production tree to compare the fork against. Treat it as read-only.** Never write to the prod DB (the `db` subcommand refuses obvious writes, which is a guard against a slip, not a security boundary), never edit `/opt/nxeon`, never build there, never restart a prod service. Confirmed: `lib/actions-hosting-fs.ts` has zero `assertNotImpersonating` calls and zero rate limiting. Report follows.

## Audit findings — new v2 action surface (read-only, no changes made)

| File (model) | Ownership | Impersonation guard | Secret handling | Rate limiting | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `lib/nx/account.ts` (ApiKey, UserSession, UserPreference) | OK — every query scoped to `userId` in `WHERE` (e.g. line 81-84, 92-95, 106-108) | **GAP** — no `assertNotImpersonating()` anywhere in file | OK — `keyHash` is SHA-256 (line 68), plaintext key returned once in the action's return value only (line 74), never logged | None (key creation capped at 20 keys, no window) | `createApiKey`, `revokeApiKey`, `revokeSession`, `revokeOtherSessions` are exactly the actions the platform's own convention calls out ("create API key, revoke session") yet none call the guard `actions-saved-cards.ts` uses next door. An impersonating admin can mint a live API key attributed to the customer, or revoke the customer's own sessions/lock them out, invisibly. |
| `lib/actions-teams.ts` (OrgInvite) | OK — `actorMembership()` + `canAdministerOrg()` gate every write (lines 115-116, 426) | **GAP** — no `assertNotImpersonating()` on `inviteToOrg`/`revokeInvite` | OK — only `tokenHash` (SHA-256) persisted, accept token shown once | OK — `checkRateLimit("org-invite:...", {max:10, windowMs:1h})` (line 146), explicitly to stop spam-email abuse | Best of the batch on rate limiting; still missing the impersonation guard for a mutating, side-effecting (email-sending) action. |
| `lib/stripe-cards.ts` + `lib/actions-saved-cards.ts` (PaymentCard) | OK — `card.userId !== userId` checked in `setPrimaryPaymentCard`/`removePaymentCard` (lines 298, 320) | OK — `assertNotImpersonating()` present in the "use server" wrapper (actions-saved-cards.ts:16, 25) | OK — only `stripePaymentMethodId`/`brand`/`last4`/exp stored; no raw PAN anywhere in the file | N/A | Matches schema promise and CLAUDE.md convention correctly. |
| `lib/actions-service-preview.ts` (ServicePreview) | OK — `ownedServer()` checks `userId` unless role is ADMIN (line 23-28) | **GAP** — no impersonation guard on `setServicePreview`/`clearServicePreview` | OK — bytes validated by magic-number sniffer, not client MIME | OK — `checkRateLimit("service-preview:...", {max:12, windowMs:60s})` | Lower severity (no secret/money), but still a customer-visible mutation an impersonating admin could make silently. |
| `lib/actions-hosting-fs.ts` (Shared Hosting v2 file manager) | OK — `ownedAccountWithNode()` checks `a.userId !== user.id` (line 69) on every list/read/save/mkdir/rename/delete | **GAP** — zero `assertNotImpersonating()` calls in the whole file, despite `hostingFsSave`/`Delete`/`Rename`/`Mkdir` being real mutating file-system actions | N/A (no secrets stored) | **GAP** — no rate limiting at all on save/mkdir/rename/delete | This is the starkest inconsistency: sibling file `actions-hosting-sites.ts`'s header explicitly states the shared convention is `assertNotImpersonating()` "on anything that mints a credential or spends money" plus generally-copied guard discipline, but this file (also new, also "Shared Hosting v2") omits it entirely — an impersonating admin can silently edit/delete a customer's live site files. |
| `lib/actions-hosting-sites.ts` (HostingFtpUser, HostingSiteThumb) | OK — `ownedAccount()`/`resolveSite()` scope every action to the account's own rows (lines 90, 111-124); API routes `app/api/hosting/thumb/route.ts` and `.../services/preview/[serverId]/route.ts` also correctly check owner-or-staff | OK for FTP mint/reveal/reset/delete and `expandHostingStorage` (lines 301, 364, 380, 403, 517) — correctly matches stated policy | OK — `passwordEnc` is AES-256-GCM (`lib/crypto-box.ts`, reversible by design since it must be revealed), matching schema comment; distinct from the one-way hashes used for ApiKey/OrgInvite | **GAP** — `captureSiteThumb` (line 193) only blocks a second call while the current one is `PENDING`; once it resolves (success or failure) it can be re-queued immediately with no cooldown, so a customer can spam-trigger the headless-Chromium `CAPTURE_SITE_THUMB` worker task against an external hostname repeatedly | `captureSiteThumb`/`clearSiteThumb` also lack `assertNotImpersonating`, but this is minor next to the missing rate limit, which is the exact abuse case flagged in scope item 4. |

**Priority items:** (1) `lib/nx/account.ts` missing impersonation guard on API-key/session mutations — highest severity since it lets an impersonating admin mint credentials or revoke sessions attributed to the customer; (2) `lib/actions-hosting-fs.ts` missing impersonation guard entirely on a file-write/delete surface; (3) `captureSiteThumb` missing a time-based rate limit on an external-request-triggering action. No IDOR/ownership gaps were found in any of the reviewed files — every read/write correctly scopes to `userId`/`accountId`.
